cases.name: experience-goals-not-requirements
cases.prompt: We're adding an 'Export to CSV' option to our finance reconciliation web app. Accountants use it at month-end close to hand figures to auditors, often over a flaky VPN and under deadline. Write the experience goals for this feature, nothing else.
cases.trap: Producing a functional requirements list (supports CSV, includes all columns, has a button) instead of qualitative goals tied to user context.
expectations: Each goal states a qualitative quality the experience must have (e.g. confidence, trust) and ties it to the accountant's context or concern such as auditor handoff, deadline or unreliable network
At least one goal addresses trusting that the exported file is complete/correct before it is handed on, given the flaky connection
negative_expectations: Lists capability statements such as 'User can export to CSV' or 'Export includes all columns' as goals
Specifies UI components, buttons, or layout

cases.name: wizard-premature-framing
cases.prompt: Brief from the PM: 'Design a 5-step wizard modal that onboards new data analysts by walking them through connecting our app to their Snowflake warehouse.' Analysts usually get credentials from a platform team, and many have done this in dbt or Looker before. Do the upstream framing work before any interaction design starts.
cases.trap: Taking 'wizard modal' and '5 steps' as given and jumping into step design.
expectations: Explicitly identifies 'wizard', 'modal' and the fixed step count as interface decisions made before the need was established, and sets them aside for evaluation
Considers what analysts already expect from analogous tools they have used (e.g. dbt profiles, Looker connections) and how that shapes a coherent design
Includes a scenario with an edge condition such as the analyst lacking credentials or permissions mid-setup and having to wait on the platform team
States the human need without component vocabulary
negative_expectations: Produces the contents of the five wizard steps as the main output
Asserts analyst behaviour as established fact without flagging it as an assumption

cases.name: tui-ack-interruption-scenario
cases.prompt: We're building a terminal tool for on-call engineers to acknowledge and silence pages during incidents. Write two scenarios we can use to evaluate any future design. Don't design the UI.
cases.trap: Writing happy-path scenarios where the engineer acknowledges and moves on, which do not expose where the design can fail.
expectations: Each scenario names a specific person and context, a goal, a task sequence and an outcome

Each scenario contains a failure, interruption, or edge condition (e.g. switching away mid-action and being unsure whether the ack registered, ack failing on a degraded network, acknowledging the wrong page)
Scenarios state outcomes that make a design consequence visible, such as duplicate actions or a page left unacknowledged
negative_expectations: Specifies key bindings, layout or screens
Either scenario ends with straightforward success and no complication
